SOURCE: ImageBind-LLM: Multi-modality Instruction Tuning. Han, Zhang, Shao, Gao, Xu, Xiao, Zhang, Liu, Wen, Guo, Lu, Ren, Wen, Chen, Yue, Li, Qiao (Shanghai AI Lab, CUHK MMLab, vivo AI Lab). arXiv 2309.03905v2 [cs.MM], 11 Sep 2023. Preprint.

COVERAGE: 81410 of 81410 chars (24 pages). I read the body to p.~18 and the end of the references, and skimmed the reference list. There are no appendices. The figures.py captions command returned nothing, so the figure captions below come from the text extraction. Table 1 and Table 2 columns are flattened in the extraction; I read the rows as printed. The tables are not mis-ordered.

CLAIMS (ranked)
- claim: Core recipe. Train only on image-text data. A frozen ImageBind image encoder gives a global feature, and a learnable "bind network" maps it into LLaMA space. The result is added to every word token at all 32 layers, scaled by a zero-initialised gate. At inference, audio, video, text and 3D inputs go through their own ImageBind encoders, with no retraining.
  number: none (gate initialised at 0)
  setup: LLaMA (non-instruction) base, ImageBind image encoder frozen. 3D uses the Point-Bind encoder.
  quote: "we only fine-tune LLaMA [11] to generate language responses conditioned on ImageBind-encoded images, after which, the model can inherently understand instructions of other modalities via the respective ImageBind encoders."
  where: Sec 3.2.1, p.4
- claim: Attention-free injection. The visual vector is added to every token rather than concatenated as a prefix and attended to. This avoids extra attention compute and eases training.
  number: Eq. 2, T_j = T_I · g_zero + T_W^j
  setup: Contrast with LLaMA-Adapter (zero-init attention), LLaVA and MiniGPT-4 (prefix concatenation). The paper gives no ablation of attention-free versus attention-based injection.
  quote: "We directly add the image feature TI with every word token at all transformer layers of LLaMA... a learnable gating factor initialized by zero"
  where: Sec 3.2.1, p.6
- claim: Bind network design. A linear projection from C_I to LLaMA's C, then 3 residual FFN-style blocks (RMSNorm, SiLU, w1/w2/w3).
  number: 3 blocks. Eq. 1: F^{i+1} = F^i + (F^i w2 · SiLU(F^i w1)) w3
  setup: ImageBind-to-LLaMA alignment
  quote: "we then cascade three projection blocks with RMSNorm [43], SiLU activation functions [44], and residual connections [45]."
  where: p.5
- claim: Only ONE visual token enters the LLM. The authors blame this for weak OCR and for hallucination. Other VLMs use 10 to 257 tokens.
  number: 1 token, versus 10 (LLaMA-Adapter), 32 (BLIP2, InstructBLIP, MiniGPT-4), 64 (Otter) and 257 (LLaVA)
  setup: Zero-shot OCR on 12 datasets, evaluated VQA-style
  quote: "both of them employ only one token for the modality feature, while the other VLMs utilize at least ten tokens for capturing visual information."
  where: Sec 4.2.2, p.11-12. Failure analysis in Sec 4.6, p.16.
- claim: OCR is far below the multi-token models. These are the paper's own numbers, so they are measured, not inferred.
  number: IIIT5K word accuracy 13.9 for ImageBind-LLM, against 80.17 (BLIP2), 83.90 (InstructBLIP), 36.30 (LLaMA-Adapter), 31.57 (LLaVA) and 5.27 (PandaGPT)
  setup: Zero-shot, VQA-style, prompt "What is written in the image?"
  quote: "IIIT5K 80.17 83.90 36.30 31.57 5.27 13.9 13.87"
  where: Table 1, p.10
- claim: ImageBind-LLM beats PandaGPT on most OCR and caption sets and is competitive on VQA. It is mixed elsewhere. PandaGPT has 90.80 on Visdial against 12.66, and InstructBLIP is far ahead on several sets.
  number: NoCaps CIDEr 30.43 (ImageBind-LLM) vs 29.65 (PandaGPT) vs 48.58 (BLIP2). OKVQA 51.66 vs 50.85 (PandaGPT). TextVQA 23.98 vs 16.42 (PandaGPT) vs 43.76 (LA). ScienceQA-IMG 55.83.
  setup: Zero-shot, 27 datasets in total
  quote: "NoCaps 48.58 46.33 41.66 33.09 29.65 30.43 29.64"
  where: Tables 1-2, p.10
- claim: On the MME perception total, ImageBind-LLM ranks third, +133.18 over PandaGPT. On cognition it scores 213.57, which is below MiniGPT-4 (292.14), LLaMA-Adapter (248.93) and PandaGPT (228.57).
  number: Perception 775.77, out of 2000. Cognition 213.57, out of 800. Existence 128.33 is the best of the models compared.
  setup: MME yes/no benchmark. Competitors are MiniGPT-4, Otter, LLaMA-Adapter, LLaVA and PandaGPT.
  quote: "Perception 866.58 483.73 972.67 502.82 642.59 775.77"
  where: Table 3, p.11. Table 4 on the same page.
- claim: The authors attribute the gain over PandaGPT partly to the bind network (versus PandaGPT's single linear projection). PandaGPT uses the stronger Vicuna base. This is speculation. There is no ablation.
  number: none
  setup: ImageBind-LLM on LLaMA vs PandaGPT on Vicuna
  quote: "PandaGPT employs a single linear projection layer for processing the ImageBind extracted feature, whereas ImageBind-LLM employs a bind network, which potentially facilitates better alignment"
  where: Sec 4.2.2, p.12
- claim: Training-free cache for inference. Non-image embeddings are pulled toward image space by retrieving the top-k nearest cached image features and mixing them in. This addresses the train/inference modality gap. It is a Tip-Adapter-style non-parametric adapter.
  number: Eq. 3-4: F_e = α·S_topk·F_value + (1−α)·F_M. The cache is 1M (CC3M) image features by default. The abstract says three million. The values of k and α are not stated.
  setup: Built with FAISS and Autofaiss
  quote: "F eM = α · StopkFvalue + (1 − α) · FM , (4) where α serves as a balance factor."
  where: Sec 3.2.3, p.8. Cache size in Sec 3.1.3 p.4 and Sec 4.1.2 p.9.
- claim: Training recipe and scale.
  number: Pre-training uses 940M noisy image-text pairs, 32 A100s, 3 epochs, batch 1024, LR 4e-4. Fine-tuning uses 8 A100s, 4 epochs, batch 32, LR 1.25e-4. LoRA rank is 16.
  setup: Pairs come from COCO, CC3M, CC12M, SBU, LAION-2B (100M filtered), COYO and MMC4 (20M). Stage 2 uses Alpaca, GPT4LLM, ShareGPT and LLaVA's 150K visual instruction data. Language-only examples get an all-zero fake image. An extra pass on MiniGPT-4's 3.5K description data cuts hallucination.
  quote: "We pre-train the model on 32 A100 GPUs for 3 epochs. The total batch size and learning rate is set to 1024 and 4e-4, respectively."
  where: Sec 4.1.2, p.9. Data in Sec 4.1.1 and Sec 3.2.2 p.6-7.
- claim: Parameter-efficient tuning in stage 2. LoRA on every linear layer, norm layers unfrozen, bias terms added. The ImageBind encoder and bind network are frozen. In stage 1 only the bind network and gates are trained.
  number: rank 16
  quote: "we add a low-rank layer for each linear layer in the transformer, where the rank is set to 16 by default. We also unfreeze all the normalization layers and add a learnable bias term"
  where: p.6
- claim: Modality mixing works by weighting embeddings and is sensitive to the ratio.
  number: Image×0.5+Audio×0.5, ×0.4/0.6 and ×0.2/0.8 give different outcomes. Only 0.4/0.6 keeps both "sky" and "dog".
  setup: Qualitative, a single example with a sky image and dog-bark audio
  quote: "modality mixup is fragile when the two modalities represent different concepts... ImageBind-LLM is sensitive to the modality mixing ratio."
  where: Sec 4.6, p.17, Fig. 13
- claim: Extensions with no quantitative eval. They are bilingual (ChineseLLaMA plus 52K Chinese instructions), any-to-any generation (Stable Diffusion, Make-An-Audio and CLIP-Forge, with cache-enhanced input), detector cascade, multi-turn chat (ShareGPT plus LLaVA conversations), GPT4Tools API control, and speech-to-text or video-detector "experts" injected as text context.
  number: none
  quote: "Although we do not have direct Chinese visual instruction data for the first vision-language training stage, we observe that our bilingual ImageBind-LLM implicitly learns the alignment between Chinese, English and multi-modality inputs"
  where: Sec 3.3, p.8

LIMITS
- No ablations. Nothing isolates the bind network, the gating, attention-free injection or the cache. There is no number for how much the cache helps or for how audio/3D quality varies. Audio, video and 3D are shown only in qualitative examples (Figs. 5-12). All quantitative evals are image-only.
- The authors concede the following. It hallucinates objects not in the image. It has only one visual token (their planned fix: more tokens). The instruction data (LLaVA) is GPT-4/expert-generated without human checks. Modality mixup is fragile. Chinese visual responses are short. It lacks fine-grained domain knowledge. It is weak on OCR and KIE.
- Compared with PandaGPT, the base LLM differs (LLaMA vs Vicuna), so the comparison is confounded.
- Hyperparameters k and α are not given. The abstract says three million cached features but the body says one million (CC3M).
- Dated: LLaMA-1 base, Sept 2023, MME-era benchmarks. Later multimodal models use multi-token patch features.

BUILDS ON: ImageBind (Girdhar et al. 2023), Point-Bind (3D), LLaMA (Touvron et al. 2023), LLaMA-Adapter (Zhang et al. 2023) and LLaMA-Adapter V2 (Gao et al. 2023) for zero-init gating and bias-norm tuning, LoRA (Hu et al., ref 15), Tip-Adapter (ref 14) for the cache, CLIP (ref 27), LLaVA (Liu et al. 2023), MiniGPT-4 (Zhu et al. 2023), PandaGPT (ref 34), BLIP-2, Alpaca, GPT4LLM (Peng et al. 2023).

CODE: none in the paper. It points to https://github.com/OpenGVLab/LLaMA-Adapter. Load-bearing equations are Eq. 1-4, quoted above.

FIGURES (captions from text extraction)
- Fig. 2 (p.5): "Training Paradigm of ImageBind-LLM." The ImageBind encoder is frozen, then the bind network, then a feature add via a zero gate into all 32 LLaMA layers. This is the best single-picture explanation of the adapter fusion.
- Fig. 3 (p.6): "Details of the Bind Network." RMSNorm, SiLU, w1/w2/w3, x3. Useful for the projector structure.
- Fig. 4 (p.7): "Cache Retrieval for Inference." (a) cache construction, (b) top-k retrieval to enhanced features. Explains the modality-gap fix.
- Fig. 1 (p.2): visual instruction models vs ImageBind-LLM (overview).
- Fig. 13 (p.19): failure cases, hallucination and mixup ratios.
- Figs. 6 and 7 (p.14-15): multi-modality and mixed-modality examples.

PROBLEMS: figures.py captions printed nothing, so the figure captions come from text extraction. Table columns are flattened, and I read them in column order as printed. The text has a typo ("FUNSD citefunsd"). The Fig. 7 text refers to "Fig. 12" (should be Fig. 7). The paper says "MiniGPT-4 can achieve the best scores", yet its perception total is below LLaMA-Adapter (866.58 vs 972.67). No embedded instructions were found in the PDF.
